criteria.semantics: A native <option> in its choice's <select>, whose text is the option's label and whose value is the option's value; with the radio hint, a native radio named by its <label for>.

keyboard.outcome: In the open list (or the radio group), move to the option.

criteria.name: The option's label, the same words as its visible text.
criteria.role: Option (menu item in a pop-up list); radio button with the radio hint.
criteria.state: Selected (checked, with the radio hint) or not.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the option's label grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the option's label whole, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <option> element.
The option submits what the model says: its value is the option's value.
The option's text is its label, so its accessible name matches what I see.
WHEN I move to the option with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its label and its place in the list (1 of 2).
WHEN I choose the option I HEAR it expressed as selected (or checked).

criteria.semantics: One focusable control per option in its choice, its label as text, the chosen option in accent-fg on accent. Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit ListBoxOption (RadioButton with the hint), selected or not.

keyboard.outcome: Focus moves to it, in reading order, and the focus ring shows.
Focus moves back to the control before it, wrapping to the last.

criteria.name: The option's label.
criteria.role: Option (list item, or radio button with the radio hint).

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the option's label grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the option's label drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the option's label at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the option's label drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) with focus following I SEE the magnifier follow the keyboard focus to the option's label.

check.statement: The option is one stop in the window's tab order, and focusing it puts the keyboard focus there.
WHEN I press Space on the focused option I SEE it chosen, set apart in accent-fg on accent.
WHEN I Tab to the option with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR its label, its place in the list and I HEAR it expressed as selected or not.

announce.api: An option of an AXList, AXSelected when chosen (AXRadioButton with AXValue 1 with the hint; AccessKit Role::ListBoxOption).
ControlType ListItem with the SelectionItem pattern, IsSelected when chosen.
ATSPI_ROLE_LIST_ITEM with STATE_SELECTABLE and STATE_SELECTED when chosen.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
